choices.consequence: You leave the sealed room, grateful for the relatively cleaner air of the library.

entities.name: Cloak of Protection
entities.description: +1 AC and saving throws, requires attunement. Found in the iron-bound chest.

scenes.dmNotes: Read the letter slowly. Pause between paragraphs. Strahd's letters are one of the great character-defining moments in Curse of Strahd — use the condescension fully. After the letter, let players register the horror that the skeleton died in here with that letter in hand, writing repeatedly to someone who never responded. That is who these cultists were. Not powerful. Just wrong.

scenes.title: Conservatory
scenes.subtitle: Second Floor, Area 10

narrationBlocks.text: A music room, or it was. The western wall holds a harpsichord of dark cherry wood, its lid propped open, strings stretched with age but unbroken. A standing silver-stringed harp occupies the corner by the rain-streaked window. Four alabaster figurines stand on marble plinths between them — dancers, arrested mid-step, carved with extraordinary detail: the turn of a wrist, the curve of a shoulder, the tilt of a chin.

As you enter the room, the harpsichord plays three notes. Not a full phrase — just three: descending, unresolved, the beginning of something that refuses to be finished. Then silence. Then, approximately thirty seconds later: the same three notes. Descending. Unresolved.

The room smells of old rosin and the particular dry cold of string instruments in an unheated space. The window has three cracks in its panes, each sealed with dark wax from the inside — someone spent time up here and was bothered by the draft.

DC 12 Performance or Arcana — If a player plays the harpsichord:

SUCCESS: They can play normally. Every melody they attempt sounds technically correct but emotionally wrong — as if the instrument is performing a perfect simulation of music without understanding why music exists. Any song a player plays: the harpsichord plays it back in a minor key, five seconds later, even if they have stopped playing.

DC 14 Arcana (follow-up, same check): The harpsichord is under a minor enchantment of the house — not a trap, not a spirit, just the house itself, maintaining the sound the room used to make.

DC 14 Perception — Examining the figurines:

SUCCESS: The fourth figurine — the one farthest from the window — has been moved from its original position. You can see the clean circle its plinth left in the dust on the floor, about eight inches from where it currently stands. Whatever moved it placed it facing the door. The figurine's carved stone face is positioned to watch the entrance.

CONSERVATORY INTERACTABLES:

• Air vent near the baseboard: DC 14 Perception to hear a faint, rhythmic sound from below — not quite a heartbeat but with similar regularity. It is the chanting in the ritual chamber far below, traveling up through the structural walls.

• Wax window seals: DC 11 Investigation reveals the wax contains embedded hair — fine, dark, possibly from the children or the nursemaid.

• No combat here. The room is a mood piece.

IF PLAYERS BREAK A FIGURINE: They take no damage. But the remaining three figurines' heads turn to look at whoever broke it. They do not move again after that. Do not explain this.

choices.consequence: You step back out into the hallway.

scenes.dmNotes: Pacing note: this is a SHORT room. Do not over-explain. The three notes on repeat, the figurine watching the door, maybe the air vent pulse — pick TWO of those three and keep the scene moving. The house builds dread through accumulation, not through long individual scenes. Five minutes maximum.

scenes.title: Balcony
scenes.subtitle: Third Floor, Area 11

narrationBlocks.text: The third floor balcony rings the stairwell, open on one side to a twenty-foot drop to the main hall below. The railing is carved mahogany, still solid. The smell here is different from the floors below: dust and dried lavender and beneath those, a sharp sting of old iron that you feel more in your sinuses than you smell.

A suit of plate armor stands against the wall at the far end of the balcony — not decorative like the second-floor suits. This one is braced in a fighting stance, halberd gripped in both its gauntleted hands at the ready, the blade angled directly toward the stairwell opening. Its wolf-face helm is different from the others: the jaw is lowered rather than fixed, giving the impression of something panting.

A baby's cry drifts across the balcony from no specific direction, rising and falling, cutting off abruptly, and then starting again after several seconds. You cannot triangulate it. It does not grow louder when you move toward any door; it does not fade when you move away.

TRIGGER FOR THE ARMOR:

The Animated Armor activates the moment any character either:
• Moves toward the Master Suite door (west side of balcony)
• Moves toward the Storage Room/Nursemaid wing (east side)
• Lingers at the balcony edge for more than 6 seconds of in-game time
• Touches the railing while looking down

The armor does not speak. It does not warn. It simply begins walking, halberd level, with mechanical precision. Run it as Animated Armor (MM p.19): AC 18, HP 33, immune to poison/psychic, vulnerable to thunder damage.
The wolf-face helm turns. The gauntlets tighten on the halberd. It moves.
narrationBlocks.encounterDetails: 1x Animated Armor (HP 33, AC 18, immune to poison and psychic, vulnerable to thunder)

narrationBlocks.text: When the armor finally stops — when the last piece of it clatters to the floor — black sap wells from the seams and crawls along the boards, pooling around the broken plates. Inside the chest cavity, where a heart would be: a crystallized rose, black and perfectly preserved, still warm to the touch.

POST-COMBAT NOTES:

The crystallized rose can be taken. It is warm, always, regardless of ambient temperature. No game mechanic — just lore. It belonged to Elisabeth Durst. It is the house's memory of her.

• Balcony edge: A player who is pushed to the edge or falls over takes 2d6 bludgeoning (20-foot fall onto marble).
• Halberd (pre-combat): If a player attempts to disarm the armor before it activates: DC 16 Sleight of Hand or the attempt triggers combat.
• Armor remnants: A longsword can sometimes be looted from the Animated Armor if it hasn't already been taken from the first floor.
With the armor destroyed, the balcony is open. Doors lead west to the master suite, east to the storage room. The staircase continues down to the second floor.

choices.consequence: You approach the double doors of the master suite.
You open the east-side door.
You descend to the second floor.

scenes.dmNotes: THIS IS THE FIRST REAL FIGHT. At level 1-2, an Animated Armor is dangerous because of its high AC — most low-level characters cannot hit it reliably. Use this to your advantage: let the first round sting. Consider having the baby crying grow louder and more distressed during the fight — the house uses it as accompaniment. The crystallized rose is a small, human, unexpected detail that lands better than it has any right to.

scenes.title: Master Suite
scenes.subtitle: Third Floor, Area 12

narrationBlocks.text: The master bedroom is a ruin. A four-poster bed in the center of the room has its canopy shredded — not by age, not by rot. By something sharp and deliberate, the cuts running in long parallel lines as if someone needed to destroy something and had only their nails. The frame is intact. The mattress has a dark stain centered where a person sleeping would be. Not old brown. Deep, oxidized red-brown.

A tall mirror occupies the east wall, framed in tarnished gilt. A wardrobe stands open on the south side, its fine clothes hanging in strips — slashed like the canopy, with the same violence, the same parallel marks. A vanity table between the wardrobe and the mirror holds combs, perfume vials, and a small locked jewelry box. The perfume vials are open. Whatever was in them has long since evaporated, but the vanity smells of something floral and oversweet, a ghost of a smell.

The room feels bruised. Like the air still carries the memory of a terrible argument — not just the sound of it but the emotional weight, the kind that lingers in rooms after people stop fighting but before anyone apologizes. No one ever apologized in this room.

DC 14 Perception — Approaching the mirror:

SUCCESS: Your reflection looks like you, but wrong. The reflection is slightly older, slightly drawn — the face hollowed, the eyes too much dark around them. The reflection's mouth moves without you moving yours. If you watch it long enough and make a DC 12 Wisdom save, you can almost parse the words. They are: 'It is cold. We are cold. Rot with us.'

A character who fails the Wisdom save (DC 12): gains the Frightened condition for 1 minute; they cannot look at the mirror and must stay more than 10 feet from it. No damage. Just dread.

DC 14 Investigation (or DC 10 if they searched the library already and had context):

SUCCESS: The jewelry box lock requires DC 15 Thieves' Tools or DC 18 Strength to force.

When they examine the wardrobe — DC 12 Investigation: In the far corner of the wardrobe bottom, behind the hanging cloth strips: a small book, hardcover, navy blue. A woman's private journal. It is Gustav's wife Elisabeth's. Three entries are legible:

1. 'G. found the new texts. Three volumes and a fragment. The fragment is different — older than anything else he has found. He won't let me see it yet. He says it requires preparation.'

2. 'The ritual takes the blood of someone willing. G. says the offering must be clean. I said I would volunteer. He looked at me the way he looks at the servants. He said that would be unnecessary.'

3. 'Walter is born. G. has decided what Walter is for. I do not object. I should. I have nothing left to object with.'

The locked jewelry box: a silver necklace with a moonstone pendant (30 gp), a gold enameled brooch in the shape of a butterfly (15 gp), and a signet ring — the inside of the band engraved with a hand and eye.
narrationBlocks.lootDetails: Silver Moonstone Necklace (30 gp) • Butterfly Brooch (15 gp) • Signet Ring (Vecna cult signet)

narrationBlocks.text:
THE JOURNAL — DELIVERY NOTES:

Do not read the journal entries aloud verbatim. Summarize them in your own words and let players ask for specifics. The emotional content is more important than the exact wording.

Key lore the journal reveals:
• The Dursts are Vecna cultists, not Strahd cultists
• Gustav found a 'fragment' of a text — likely a piece of Vecna's instructions or a creation manual for the Eldritch Eye
• Walter was deliberately intended to be a sacrifice or a vessel from before birth
• Elisabeth knew. She chose not to object. This makes her worse than a victim.
A door on the south wall leads to the master bathroom.

choices.consequence: You push the bathroom door open.
You step back out.

scenes.dmNotes: This room tells the full Durst family horror in three journal entries and one mirror. The violence in the room (the shredded canopy, the slashes in the wardrobe) was done by Elisabeth and is not explained anywhere. Players should be left to figure out whether it was despair, rage, or something the ritual required. Leave it ambiguous. The mirror is the best pure horror beat on this floor — use it gently.

scenes.title: Bathroom
scenes.subtitle: Third Floor, Area 13

narrationBlocks.text: A bathroom with cold marble tile and a claw-footed copper tub dominating the center. The tub is stained a deep brown along its inner basin — not from water but from something that sat in it and oxidized over years. A rusted copper kettle rests beside the tub on a wooden stool. The mirror above the washbasin has been covered with a single sheet of black cloth, knotted at the top. Someone did not want to see their reflection.

The smell of copper is immediate and specific. There is no water in the tub. There is no water anywhere in the room. Whatever stained the basin evaporated long ago, leaving only the ghost of a smell that the copper amplified and kept.

IF A CHARACTER LOOKS INTO THE TUB:

Tell them they see the basin is dry and stained and at the very bottom, barely visible under the discoloration, something has been scratched into the copper with something sharp: '17 words.' Nothing else. Seventeen words were scratched here and then erased, leaving only the count.

This is Elisabeth's work. The seventeen words she scratched were, at some point, removed by the house. If a player makes a DC 18 Arcana check on the scratch marks, they can feel residual emotion — cold, absolute terror, not rage and not grief. Something beyond those. The house ate the words.

DC 12 Investigation — Removing the black cloth from the mirror:

If they take the cloth off: the mirror shows the room normally, except that behind the character looking into it, seated in the tub, there is a woman. Gaunt, dark-haired, in a ruined gown, submerged to the chest in water that is not there. Her eyes are closed. When a character blinks: she is gone. The tub is empty.

No attack. No damage. No save required. Just the image, present for one moment, and then not.

choices.consequence: You step out of the bathroom.

scenes.dmNotes: This room exists for two things: atmosphere and the "17 words" mystery that never resolves. Horror fiction is full of things that almost make sense and then don't quite. The mystery of what those seventeen words were is more disturbing than anything you could write in them. Keep it under three minutes. It is a punctuation mark, not a chapter.

scenes.title: Storage Room
scenes.subtitle: Third Floor, Area 14

narrationBlocks.text: A cramped room packed with household stores: folded sheets, spare wool blankets, bars of lye soap stacked by size, extra candles in bundles. A shelf holds labeled bottles of cleaning solution and polishing blends. Everything is meticulous. Someone cared about the order of small domestic things in this house even while larger, terrible things happened below.

A heavy-bristled broom leans in the corner beside the door. The bristles are clean. The handle is smooth with use. As you cross the threshold, the broom falls away from the wall, catches itself — there is no catch, there is nothing — and comes straight at the nearest face.

TRIGGER: The broom animates the moment a character steps fully inside the room — even one step past the threshold counts. There is no Perception check, no warning. It simply moves. Run as Broom of Animated Attack: AC 15, HP 17, speed 30, immune to poison and psychic.

POST-COMBAT: The broom does not die with a visual. It simply stops moving, mid-air, and drops. The bristles splinter on impact. A character who inspects the remnants finds, embedded in the spine of the broom handle, a thin strip of parchment covered in infernal script too small to read without Thieves' Tools or magnification; DC 15 Arcana confirms it is a command word binding — the broom has been enchanted to obey whoever wrote this, and the command was written in Infernal.
The broom launches from the corner at eyebrow level.
narrationBlocks.encounterDetails: 1x Broom of Animated Attack (HP 17, AC 15, immune to poison and psychic)

narrationBlocks.text: A small door on the south side leads to the Nursemaid's Suite.

choices.consequence: You back out of the storage room.
You pass through the south door.

scenes.dmNotes: This is the house's most deliberately mundane jump scare. A broom. There is something wonderfully absurd about it — a house full of ancient evil and one of its attacks is a domestic cleaning implement. Play it with absolute seriousness. The infernal enchantment detail turns it dark again immediately after. The high AC (15) makes it frustrating for low-level characters, which is by design.

scenes.title: Nursemaid's Suite
scenes.subtitle: Third Floor, Area 15

narrationBlocks.text: The temperature drops when you open this door. Not gradually — immediately, sharply, like stepping into a root cellar. Frost edges the windowpanes. Your breath mists, for the first time since you entered this house. A simple servant's bed sits in one corner, and in the center of the room, a wooden crib draped in tattered black lace. Whatever was in the crib is long gone. The lace moves very slightly, as if disturbed by an air current that is not there.

A full-length silver mirror stands beside the crib, its surface unclouded, perfectly clear. In the mirror: the crib is not empty. In the reflection, swaddled in clean lace and breathing, is a perfect infant boy, eyes closed, clutching a small wooden rattle. His chest moves with the rhythm of a sleeping child. In the room, the crib is empty. In the mirror, he sleeps.
Silence. Absolute silence, as if the room finally stopped pretending the baby would cry. The cold has weight. It presses.

DC 14 Perception — Watching the mirror image carefully:

SUCCESS: The infant in the mirror opens his eyes. They are not infant eyes. They are old. Black, and old, and patient, and they are looking directly at whoever made this check. The infant's mouth opens. No sound comes from the room, but in the mirror's reflection, you can see the shape the mouth makes:

'WHY DID YOU LEAVE ME HERE?'

Then the eyes close. The infant sleeps again in the reflection. In the room, the crib is and has always been empty.

SECRET DOOR:

A DC 12 Investigation check (or DC 10 if the character is actively searching the walls) reveals a seam in the north wall — a hidden door, well-fitted, flush with the plaster. Opening it reveals a narrow staircase leading up to the attic. This is the only path to the attic that does not require the padlocked door from Area 20 (which requires the key from the library).

SPECTER TRIGGER:

The Nursemaid's Specter activates when ANY of the following happen:
• A character touches the crib or removes the lace
• A character touches the mirror
• A character examines the mirror for longer than 30 in-game seconds without looking away
• A character finds the hidden door (the specter considers this as someone intending to go further in)

The Specter is the nursemaid — she did not escape this house. She loved Walter genuinely. She hates what was done to him and cannot distinguish between 'caused his suffering' and 'is present in the room where his ghost rests'. Everyone in the room is a threat to her.

Statblock: HP 22, AC 12, Speed 0/50 fly (hover), Intangible, incorporeality, life drain (2d6 necrotic on hit, target must DC 10 Con save or max HP reduced by the same amount until long rest — THIS IS DANGEROUS AT LEVEL 2.

The temperature drops further, if that is possible. The frost on the windows spreads, crawling inward. The mirror goes dark. And then the nursemaid steps through it — not out of it, through it, as if the glass were smoke. She is very tall. She is very thin. Her jaw hangs slightly open. Her eyes are two pale reflections of the frost on the glass. She does not scream. She does not speak. She opens her hands toward you as if to take something from you, and her hands are larger than they should be.
The nursemaid's specter lunges, her touch draining warmth from bone.
narrationBlocks.encounterDetails: 1x Specter (HP 22, AC 12, Life Drain: 2d6 necrotic, Con DC 10 or max HP reduced — potentially lethal at level 1-2)

narrationBlocks.text:
MANAGING THE SPECTER'S LETHALITY:

At level 1-2, the Specter's max HP reduction can kill a character who fails two saves in a row. You have options:

• If a character drops to 0 max HP from her drain: the specter pauses. She looks at the fallen character. She appears, for a moment, genuinely grieved rather than predatory. Then continues.

• Retreat option: if the party flees through the hidden door, she does not follow past the nursery door. She stays with the crib.

• If someone shows the characters' compassion toward the crib (speaks gently to the room, addresses Walter's memory): the specter pauses for one round, flickering with something that isn't rage. This lets a round of healing/repositioning happen.

• Narrative mercy: if a character is about to die from max HP reduction, have the specter shift her attention to a different target for one round — 'she didn't choose this victim specifically, she's confused and lashing at everything.'

choices.consequence: You retreat back toward the balcony.

choices.text: Take the Hidden Stairs Up to the Attic
choices.consequence: You find the hidden door and take the narrow stairs upward.

scenes.dmNotes: This is the most dangerous room in the house above the dungeon. Prepare the party survival options mentally before this fight. The baby in the mirror saying 'WHY DID YOU LEAVE ME HERE' needs to be delivered calmly, matter-of-factly, no drama added. Restraint is how this line hits. Don't over-play it.

scenes.title: Attic Hall
scenes.subtitle: Attic, Area 16

narrationBlocks.text: The attic is a different house entirely. No carpets. No carved panels. No pretense. Bare plank floors, bare timber walls, cobwebs in every corner, the raw smell of old wood and dust and something biological that has been sealed here long enough to stop having a distinct smell and just become part of the air. The ceiling slopes sharply to the roofline overhead, making the hall feel like a throat.

The temperature has equalized. The attic is not cold the way the nursemaid's suite was cold. It is simply still. The kind of still that descends on a room that has not been entered in a very long time, where even the dust does not move without encouragement.

A heavy padlocked door stands at the far end of the hall. The padlock is iron, thick, relatively new compared to the rest of the house — placed here deliberately, recently, by whoever cared about keeping something behind it secured. On either side of it, two other doors lead into storage on the left and a spare room on the right.

DC 11 Perception — Looking at the padlocked door:

SUCCESS: The door has scratch marks on the inside face — visible at the bottom gap between door and floor. Something wanted out from inside. The scratches are at floor level, the height a small child might make. They are old.

ATTIC HALL CONNECTIONS:
• Left door → Spare Bedroom (Area 17)
• Right door → Storage Room (Area 18)
• Padlocked door → Children's Room (Area 20) [Iron Key from Library, Area 8]
• Back through the nursemaid's stairs → Third Floor (Area 15)

PADLOCK:

• Iron Key from the Library desk (Area 8): opens it automatically.
• DC 16 Thieves' Tools to pick: the lock is good quality.
• DC 20 Athletics to force the bar: possible but loud — the house will respond by dropping the temperature 10 degrees and having the shadows in every room deepen.
• The padlock was placed here by Gustav Durst to keep the children in.

choices.consequence: You enter the spare bedroom.
You enter the storage room.
You use the iron key on the padlock. It opens.
You take the narrow stairs back down to the third floor.

scenes.dmNotes: Attic pacing note: the horror here is simpler and more personal than the ornate dread of the lower floors. The attic is where the house stops performing elegance. It is just bare wood and cold and what was done to children. Keep descriptions spare — the lack of ornamentation is itself the horror.

scenes.title: Spare Bedroom
scenes.subtitle: Attic, Area 17

narrationBlocks.text: A spare room. A cot with a straw mattress. A washstand. A small oval window looking out over the village street, its glass wavy with age, the misty village below barely visible. On the windowsill sits a porcelain doll — perfectly upright, hands folded in its lap, face forward. Its painted smile is wrong in the way that painted smiles on dolls are always slightly wrong: too wide, too fixed, showing too many teeth for the size of the face.
The doll has been here long enough that the windowsill has grown slightly darker under it. It has been placed here deliberately and left. No child played with this doll. It was positioned.

DC 12 Investigation — Examining the doll:

SUCCESS: The doll's dress has a small stylized eye embroidered at the collar hem — a very old symbol for warding against the evil eye. But the eye is inverted in the embroidery. An inverted ward doesn't protect — it invites. Someone embroidered this protection wrong on purpose.

The doll's head can be removed: inside, packed in wool, is a small brass locket. The locket contains a tiny painted portrait of a woman on one side and a tiny painted portrait of an infant on the other. The woman is not Elisabeth Durst. The infant looks like any infant. On the back of the locket: 'For when he comes into his power.'

The doll is not magical. The locket is not cursed. The room contains no encounter. This is pure atmosphere and lore seeding.

The 'he' in the locket inscription refers to Walter. The woman is the nursemaid. She made this locket herself and placed it in the doll — a small act of genuine love in a house that was never oriented toward love. This detail makes the nursemaid's specter hit differently if players got here after that encounter.

choices.consequence: You step back into the hall.
You find a connecting door.

scenes.dmNotes: Three minutes, maximum. The doll and the locket do their work quickly. Do not linger here.

scenes.title: Empty Bedroom
scenes.subtitle: Attic, Area 19

narrationBlocks.text: A room with nothing in it. No bed, no furniture, no stored materials. Floor to wall to sloped ceiling. Bare, unfinished, empty. You search it because that is what people do when they enter rooms in haunted houses. There is nothing to find.

The absence feels intentional. As if whatever was in this room was removed to make a point, or taken away as punishment, or never placed here because this room was always meant to be punishment itself.

DC 13 Arcana — Detecting magic in the empty room:

SUCCESS: There is a very faint residue. Not active magic — the memory of magic, the kind that lingers in a space where a ritual has been performed repeatedly over a long period of time. Not a necromantic residue. Something older and harder to classify. The resonance is structured — call-and-response patterns, like a prayer given back as an echo.

This room was used for devotional practice. Vecna is called through repetition, not ceremony. This was where the cultist who died in the secret room below came to pray.

choices.consequence: You step back through the connecting door.

scenes.dmNotes: The power of this room is that it has nothing in it. Do not add things to it. Describe the nothing. Then the one perception that something WAS here. Then move on.

scenes.title: Attic Storage Room
scenes.subtitle: Attic, Area 18

narrationBlocks.text: A storage room. Broken furniture in pieces against the walls — a chair with two legs, a bedside table with a shattered top, a mirror frame with no glass. Old paintings stacked with their faces to the wall. An iron-bound trunk occupies the center of the space, heavy enough that it has left impression marks in the floor around it where it has settled over years.

DC 12 Investigation — Turning the paintings to face outward:

SUCCESS: Every painting is of the same subject — the Death House itself, rendered from slightly different angles and at slightly different times. The paintings span at least three decades based on stylistic variation and the aging of the house: the first shows it new-built and pristine, each subsequent one shows more decay. The last painting, the most recent, shows the house as it appears now — but with light in every window and the silhouettes of figures inside each frame. None of those figures are human in proportion.

DC 12 Investigation or DC 14 Perception — Examining the trunk:

SUCCESS: The trunk lid is unlatched. Inside, coiled carefully on top of old linens: a human skeleton. An adult, female, based on bone structure. Arranged with care — not discarded, not posed dramatically, simply placed as if someone took the time to fold the bones together neatly. A nursemaid's uniform, mended and clean, is draped over the remains like a shroud.

This is the nursemaid. This is what was done with her body after she died.

THE NURSEMAID'S BONES:

If players have already fought the Nursemaid's Specter (Area 15), this is the gut-punch ending of that story. Say: 'You recognize the uniform. It is exactly the dress the specter was wearing.'

This is the full context: The nursemaid died in this house, unacknowledged. The cultists who killed her folded her remains neatly into a trunk where she would not be found. Her ghost awoke and defended the nursery, not understanding that Walter was already dead. She has been there ever since.

If players find this BEFORE they encounter the specter: they know the specter's story before they meet her. It changes the encounter — give players who speak to the specter about her bones a DC 12 Persuasion option to delay her attack for one round while she processes what they are saying.

SECRET DOOR:

DC 13 Investigation (or DC 10 if the character mentions looking at the wall beside the trunk): A wooden panel in the north wall is hinged. Behind it: a narrow spiral staircase descending 50 feet into darkness. This is the main attic path to the dungeon level (Area 21).

choices.consequence: You step back into the hall.
You find the panel and open it, revealing stairs into darkness.

scenes.dmNotes: The paintings and the nursemaid's remains are two of the best quiet horror moments in the attic. Do not rush either. The nursemaid reveal — especially if they've already fought her specter — is one of the most emotionally effective beats in the module. It asks players to feel something for the ghost they just destroyed.

scenes.title: Children's Room
scenes.subtitle: Attic, Area 20

narrationBlocks.text:
The padlock opens without resistance. The door swings inward. And you see:

Two small skeletons lying in the center of the floor, side by side, their hands touching. Not posed — they fell here, or were laid here. Around them, the room that was built for them: two small beds with wooden headboards painted with rabbits and flowers, a toy chest with a broken hinge, a bookshelf with illustrated children's books, a dollhouse on a table in the corner.

The dollhouse is a perfect scale replica of the house you are standing in. Every room is present. Every detail is correct — the red marble staircase, the chandeliers, the wolf armor, the family portrait. When you look through the tiny windows of the dollhouse attic: there is a tiny replica of this room. And in that room, two tiny figures.
The room is cold. Not unnaturally cold — just the cold of a space that has not been heated since the children died. The drafts from the roofline move here. The house here is not sealed.

DC 11 Investigation — Examining the dollhouse:

SUCCESS: The figures in the dollhouse's attic room are not carved wooden dolls like the rest. They are made from cloth and stuffed. Someone took the time to make them look like specific children — the older one with dark hair, the younger one with lighter hair, smaller. The miniature dollhouse within the dollhouse also contains miniature figures. The recursion does not end at three levels — the fourth is too small to make out. But it continues.

Also: In the dollhouse dungeon level, one tiny room contains a miniature altar. On the altar: a tiny metallic sphere, smaller than a pin head, that catches light in a way that is not possible for an object that size.

DC 12 Investigation — Searching the room:

SUCCESS: Under the toy chest: a small iron box, unrusted, warm to the touch. Inside the iron box: two small pouches of bone and ash — the remains of Rose and Thornboldt, removed from wherever they died and stored here. Also: a child's drawing on folded paper. Two stick figures holding hands under what might be a sun, or an eye. Signed, in large unsteady letters: 'ROSE AND THORN WE ARE HERE.'

The ghost children appear. Not dramatically — they are simply there, at the room's threshold, looking at the skeletons on the floor. Rose has her hand pressed over her mouth. Thorn presses against her side, eyes down.
Is that us?
narrationBlocks.speaker: Thorn
narrationBlocks.emotion: Very small voice. He already knows the answer.

narrationBlocks.text: Yes. Those are our bones. We... have been here a very long time, I think.
narrationBlocks.speaker: Rose
narrationBlocks.emotion: Trying to be gentle for Thorn. Not quite managing it.

narrationBlocks.text:
GHOST CHILDREN SCENE:

Rose and Thorn want to be at rest. They cannot achieve it themselves — the house trapped them here. But if the party:

1. Takes their remains and buries them in the Family Crypts (Area 23) in the dungeon
2. Treats the burial with dignity rather than treating it as a puzzle to solve

...the children achieve peace. Their ghost forms fade with a simple, direct 'thank you' to whoever carried them. No drama. No fanfare. Just: gone.

REWARDS:
• Inspiration to every character present at the burial
• Rose's ghost will briefly appear in the dungeon stairwell as the party passes and point in the direction of the safer path through the dungeon — a single, silent gesture, then gone
• The house becomes 5 degrees warmer in all rooms immediately after the burial, as if exhaling

If the party IGNORES the children or refuses: no combat, no penalty. But Rose and Thorn will appear one more time — at the ritual chamber door — and watch the party go in. They do not say anything. That might be worse.

DOLLHOUSE META PUZZLE:

The dollhouse mirrors the house in real time: if the party moves a piece of furniture in the actual house, the dollhouse updates. If they look into the dungeon rooms of the dollhouse, they can see a crude preview of what those rooms contain (DM's discretion on detail level — the dollhouse shows major features like altars and statues but not specific creature positions).

This is optional complexity for players who engage with it. Do not force the puzzle. Let it reward curious players.

choices.consequence: You carry whatever you have decided to carry and leave the children's room.

choices.text: Descend Via Hidden Stairs (through Storage Room)
choices.consequence: You take the spiral stairs toward the dungeon.

entities.name: Rose (Ghost)
entities.description: The ghost of Rosavalda Durst. Appears near the children's room. Wants to rest but cannot alone.

entities.name: Thorn (Ghost)
entities.description: The ghost of Thornboldt Durst. Stays close to his sister. Cried when he asked if the skeletons were them.

scenes.dmNotes: The strongest emotional scene in the entire module. Two children's skeletons on the floor. Their ghost asking "Is that us?" Your table should be quiet for this. Encourage players to react in character. The dollhouse reveal — a tiny altar with a tiny metallic sphere — is the final Vecna seed of the upper house, paying off when the party finds the Eldritch Eye on Delvin's body below.

scenes.title: Secret Spiral Staircase
scenes.subtitle: Attic to Dungeon, Area 21

narrationBlocks.text: The spiral staircase is stone — narrow, without a handrail, the steps worn smooth from use. Moisture runs down the walls in thin rivulets. The smell changes with every few steps of descent: first the attic's dry dust, then something woodsy and organic, then something older. Older than wood. Mud and limestone and something underneath that, something that does not have a good name.

The staircase takes fifty feet of descent to deliver you to the bottom. Fifty feet. The house is three stories. The dungeon is beneath the house. The math does not add up in any normal way. You have gone farther down than the building above you goes up.

The descent feels longer than its length. Each footstep is louder than it should be. Your light seems to advance more slowly than you do. The chanting, faint before, is thicker here — below you, resonant through the stone walls, the same phrase repeated in a language that sounds old and deliberately private.

DARKNESS NOTE:

The dungeon is completely dark. Characters without darkvision or a light source are Blinded on the dungeon level. Describe the first step off the stairs onto dirt floor carefully — the texture change from stone to mud under their boots, the ceiling close and irregular above them, the smell.

The chanting: 'He is the ancient. He is the land. He is the eye that does not close.' It does not repeat identically — each cycle varies slightly, suggesting either many voices or one voice that has been going long enough to lose coherence.
The stairs empty onto a narrow dirt corridor braced with rotting timber. The dungeon stretches ahead: low ceilings, packed earth, the smell of deep underground. The chanting is everywhere.

choices.consequence: Your boots hit damp earth. The dungeon begins.
You retreat back to the attic storage room.

scenes.dmNotes: The geometry note — going farther down than the building is tall — is the pivot moment where players feel the domain at work. The house exists in a place that does not follow normal architectural physics. Deliver this matter-of-factly: "The math does not add up." Then move on. The mystery is more effective than an explanation.

scenes.title: Dungeon Level
scenes.subtitle: Area 22

narrationBlocks.text: The stairs drop into a narrow, rough-hewn passage. The floor is muddy. The walls are held by rotting timbers that look ready to snap. The smell of decay is immediate and overpowering.
A distant, rhythmic thud echoes through the tunnels, like a slow heartbeat. A low, melodic chant rises and falls somewhere far below.
The chant is from the ritual chamber. It is muffled and directionless here. There are no lights in the dungeon; darkvision or a torch is required.
The passage splits. One route angles west toward a low ceiling and stone alcoves. Another turns north into a wider chamber.

choices.consequence: You head down the western passage.
You head north into the wider alcove area.

scenes.dmNotes: Set the tone immediately. The house was strange; the dungeon is a tomb.

scenes.title: Family Crypts
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 23

narrationBlocks.text: Four heavy stone crypts sit beneath low arches. Their slabs are coated in gray web-like fungus.
DC 10 Investigation - The names beneath the fungus read: Gustav Durst, Elisabeth Durst, Rosavalda Durst, and Thorvalda Durst.

Crypts:
- Gustav and Elisabeth: empty. They became ghasts elsewhere.
- Rose and Thorn: empty, waiting. If the party lays the children's bones here, award inspiration and a moment of peace.
From the north comes a wet scuttling sound, like dozens of tiny legs in mud.

choices.consequence: You follow the strange sound.
You back out of the crypts.

scenes.dmNotes: Burying the children is the main redemptive act in this module. Reward it openly.

scenes.title: Cult Quarters
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 24

narrationBlocks.text: Dozens of rotting straw pallets line the walls. The smell here is appalling - old sweat, filth, and decay. Swarms of bloated centipedes roil over the bedding, feeding on rot.
Trigger: As soon as the party steps fully in or shines bright light, the swarms surge forward.
Centipede swarms spill across the walls and ceiling.
A heavy wooden table stands in the center. An iron-bound chest sits on it. A locked iron gate blocks the north passage.
Gate: Opens with the heavy iron key from the secret room (Area 9), or DC 16 Thieves' Tools, or DC 20 Athletics to bend.
Inside the chest: a silvered shortsword, three Potions of Healing, 140 sp and 22 gp, and a carved bone trinket.
narrationBlocks.lootDetails: Silvered Shortsword, 3x Potion of Healing, 140 sp, 22 gp

choices.consequence: The gate screeches open, revealing stairs down.
You head away from the quarters.

scenes.dmNotes: Gross resource drain. The iron gate is a major chokepoint if they missed the key.

scenes.title: Hidden Shrine
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 26

narrationBlocks.text: Niches line the walls, each holding a life-sized wooden statue of a ghoul. Their painted claws are stained dark. A rough stone altar sits in the center, black with old blood.
The chanting is louder here, vibrating up through the floor. The ghoul statues cast twitching shadows.
Trigger: Four real ghouls hide among the statues. If a character nears the altar or touches a statue, the ghouls leap out.
Ghouls burst from the niches, shrieking and clawing.
Behind the altar, a fresh corpse slumps against the wall.
It is Delvin Fearnehart. His leathers are torn, a gaping wound carved into his chest. His eyes are wide in terror.
DC 10 Medicine - He has been dead at least a week. The last time you saw him was hours ago.
Inside the wound is a heavy metallic orb the size of an apple - the Eldritch Eye. It throbs faintly, in time with the dungeon heartbeat.
Delvin's journal is stuffed in his boot. It warns about a corpse-like master and a stolen focus called the Eldritch Eye.

choices.consequence: You head toward the smell of the centipedes.
You carefully continue east.
You head back to the spiral staircase.

entities.name: Delvin Fearnehart
entities.description: His corpse. Proof of the time anomaly.

entities.name: Eldritch Eye
entities.description: A metallic orb that pulses like a heartbeat.

scenes.dmNotes: This is the biggest narrative payload in the dungeon. Delvin's death establishes the time skip. The Eye bridges to the next adventure.

scenes.title: The Prison
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 27

narrationBlocks.text: Four cramped cells line a damp corridor. Rusted bars are streaked with old gore. Inside, chained skeletons slouch against the walls.
The chanting is loud now, echoing from below: 'He is the ancient. He is the land.'
One skeleton wears a jagged iron ring. If a character removes it, the skeleton animates and attacks.
A chained skeleton lurches forward, clawing.
Stone stairs lead down into deeper darkness.

choices.consequence: You walk back past Delvin's body.
You take the stairs deeper.

scenes.dmNotes: A minor trap encounter and a loud reminder of the chant below.

scenes.title: Darklord's Shrine
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 28

narrationBlocks.text: A wide vaulted chamber. Two inches of black water cover the floor. A raised dais holds a statue of a tall aristocrat with a wolf at his side. A crystal orb rests in his left hand.
Drips from the ceiling sound like a slow clock. The cold here bites.
Trigger: When a character steps onto the dais or touches the orb, five Shadows peel from the floor and attack.
Shadows rise from the water, draining strength.
The crystal orb is worth 25 gp and can serve as an arcane focus. It may also allow Strahd to watch through it at times.
A portcullis leads west to the master crypts. Heavy doors to the south lead to the ritual chamber.

choices.consequence: You wade through the water to the west.
You push open the heavy double doors.

scenes.dmNotes: Shadows can be deadly at low levels. Spread their attacks out if needed.

scenes.title: Master Crypt
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 29

narrationBlocks.text: Two stone sarcophagi sit open, their lids shoved aside. The smell of rot is immediate and thick.
Gustav and Elisabeth Durst are ghasts here. They ambush from behind the sarcophagi.
You will serve the Master... your blood for his glory...
narrationBlocks.speaker: Gustav Durst (ghast)
narrationBlocks.emotion: Gurgling, insane

narrationBlocks.text: The Dursts attack, claws dripping filth.
Among the mud: a signet ring and a scroll of Protection from Evil and Good.
narrationBlocks.lootDetails: Signet Ring, Scroll of Protection from Evil and Good

choices.consequence: You wade back into the statue room.
You check the small, muddy cave.

scenes.dmNotes: This is a mini-boss fight. Emphasize that these are the parents from the portrait upstairs.

scenes.title: Reliquary
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 30

narrationBlocks.text: A cramped cave. Stinking water drips from the ceiling. A rusted iron chest sits in the mud among disgusting relics: a mummified hand, a jar of pickled eyes, a whip braided with hair.
The chest is untrapped and unlocked.
Inside: 300 cp, 150 sp, and a Potion of Greater Healing.
narrationBlocks.lootDetails: 300 cp, 150 sp, Potion of Greater Healing

choices.consequence: You slide back through the fissure.

scenes.dmNotes: A quick loot grab off the beaten path.

scenes.title: The Ritual Chamber
scenes.subtitle: Dungeon, Area 38

narrationBlocks.text:
The tunnel opens and the chanting stops. Mid-syllable. Total silence.

A forty-foot-square room of smooth masonry. Water covers most of the floor, two feet deep, black and still. Stone ledges line the walls. In the center, stairs climb from the dark water to an octagonal stone dais.

Above the dais, rusty chains dangle from the ceiling, positioned to hold someone upright facing down. Below the chains sits a stone altar, carved with grasping hands and open mouths, stained dark brown. To the west, a breach in the wall leads to a natural cave where a massive heap of rotting vegetation lies perfectly still.
TRIGGER THE BEAT: The moment any character steps onto the dais, read the next block.

The chanting returns — not distant, here. Thirteen robed figures materialize on the stone ledges. Each holds a torch burning with black flame that draws light inward. Beneath the hoods: nothing. They chant in unison: 'One must die. One must die. One must die.'
DC 11 Religion or Insight — A sacrifice: any living creature must die on the altar. The spirits don't care what kind.
Passive Perception — Five or six of the apparitions bear a mark on the back of their spectral hands: a hand with an eye in the center of the palm. It looks grown, not tattooed.

VECNA SEED: The eye-in-palm is Vecna's mark. Do not name it. They will see it again in the Nest of the Eldritch Eye.

The apparitions are intangible. Any living creature works for the sacrifice (rat, spider, familiar, NPC). Blood must touch the altar.
He is the Ancient. He is the Land...
narrationBlocks.speaker: Cult Apparitions
narrationBlocks.emotion: If sacrifice is made. The chant becomes a murmur, sinking into the stone as they fade.

narrationBlocks.text:
BRANCH A: SACRIFICE MADE
The house is appeased. The room empties. The house above exhales, pressure releasing from timbers. No gauntlet. Doors work. The exit is clean.
Lorghoth the Decayer... we awaken thee!
narrationBlocks.speaker: Cult Apparitions
narrationBlocks.emotion: If the party refuses or tries to leave the dais.

narrationBlocks.text: If refused: The refuse in the western cave moves. What you thought was dead vegetation drags itself upright — an eight-foot-tall mass of roots, tendrils, and rot. No face. Just hunger.
Lorghoth the Decayer advances to feed.

BRANCH B: SACRIFICE REFUSED
The Shambling Mound advances slowly. It does not leave the dungeon. If the party flees, the house wakes up and the Gauntlet begins in the escape scene. If they circle back and make a sacrifice, Lorghoth returns to the cave.

choices.consequence: You run back through the double doors.
The house begins to actively kill you.
The house lets you leave in peace.

scenes.dmNotes: Climax fight. The flesh mound can kill a low-level party fast. Advise running. The Vecna hand symbol here is a critical visual seed for the next adventure.

scenes.title: The Escape
scenes.subtitle: Death House - The Exit

narrationBlocks.text:
IF APPEASED (SACRIFICE MADE): The house lets you go. The tunnels are quiet. Each floor is exactly as you left it, but the air is thinner — as if the house's interest in you has faded. The front doors open without resistance. Outside: grey sky, cold air, gravel. (Skip the Gauntlet entirely)

IF REFUSED (NO SACRIFICE): As you climb back up, the house wakes. The facade of beauty is gone. It is showing you what it actually is.

THE GAUNTLET HAZARDS (Active on all floors):
• Bricked Windows: Every window is sealed with stone from inside. No escape.
• Scythe Blades: Razor-sharp pendulum blades swing in repeating arcs filling each doorframe. (DC 15 Acrobatics to pass unharmed. DC 15 Intelligence to time it. Fail = 2d10 slashing)
• Poison Smoke: Every fireplace/stove belches thick black smoke. Burns eyes and lungs. (DC 10 Con save per room. Fail = 1d10 poison damage per turn)
• Rat Swarms: Wall splinters release hundreds of rats. (AC 5, 5 HP per section. Or DC 10 Strength to smash through)
(SCYTHE BLADES) The doors are gone. In every doorway, a blade swings in a repeating arc — razor-sharp, pendulum-steady. The edge gleams, and each swing fills the frame completely.
(POISON SMOKE) Every fireplace and stove belches thick black smoke that hangs at shoulder height. The smell is acrid — chemical, almost alive.
(RAT SWARMS) The wall splinters and a tide of rats pours out — hundreds, grey fur and black eyes and small sharp teeth, spilling from the walls like a hemorrhage.
The oaken front doors. For one breath you think they might be sealed — that this house has decided you'll die in it. You push. They open.

Outside: grey sky. Cold air. Gravel crunching beneath boots that have been in places boots shouldn't go. Death House stands behind you — not angry, not satisfied. Disappointed. As if you were a meal that wasn't worth finishing.
The fog at the village edges has thinned. The boarded shops and silent tavern stand in grey light with the patience of things that know they'll be needed again.

Give this moment weight. They survived. They are Level 3. Let them feel it before moving to the Bridge.
If anyone looks back at the house: it looks exactly as it did when they entered. Pristine. Inviting. The gate is slightly ajar.

choices.consequence: You walk toward the only opening in the fog.

scenes.dmNotes: Run the gauntlet fast and frantic if they chose not to sacrifice. If they did sacrifice, let them walk out in eerie, quiet safety.

scenes.title: Return to Neverwinter
scenes.subtitle: The Bridge Through the Mists

narrationBlocks.text: The fog at the edges of Barovia begins to move — not retreating, opening. Like a door. Like hands parting. You walk toward it. There is no other direction. Gravel becomes cobblestone. The cold thins. The weight of the village lifts from your shoulders in stages.
You walk through the fog. Same as before — directionless, timeless. But shorter this time, as if whatever brought you there has decided you're finished and wants you gone.

The fog shreds apart violently, as if something on the other side lost patience. Light hits you like a wall. City sounds: a blacksmith's hammer, a distant bell, the murmur of a crowd. The smell of horse dung, smoke, baking bread, and the mineral tang of the sea.
You are standing at the western gate of Neverwinter. The sun is high.
Oi! Where'd you lot come from? That gate's been closed all week.
narrationBlocks.speaker: Gate Guard
narrationBlocks.emotion: Surprised, suspicious

narrationBlocks.text:
When players speak to the guard, establish that TIME HAS PASSED. Several weeks have passed since they left, not just a few days.

Guard info:
- Fog rolled in thick about two weeks back.
- The Commander ordered the gate sealed until it cleared yesterday.
- There's been trouble in the western district — city watch found bodies. 'Cult business, they reckon.'

The city looks the same, but the light is different. The trees along the Dolphin Bridge have fewer leaves. Market stalls that sold summer fruit now sell root vegetables. Time has passed — not days. Weeks.

choices.consequence: You step through the gate into Neverwinter.

scenes.dmNotes: Don't belabor the time skip. The guard's dialogue establishes it. Let the players ask one or two questions, then move to the scream.

scenes.title: Kevori's Scream
scenes.subtitle: Neverwinter Alleyway

narrationBlocks.text: You've taken twenty steps into the city when an anguished scream erupts from a nearby alley. Raw, broken — the sound of someone discovering something they already feared. The sound of someone who held onto hope for weeks and has just let it drop. You round the corner.

Kevori Fearnehart kneels in the dirt. She is thinner than when you last saw her — hair loose, unwashed, leather armor scuffed in ways it wasn't before. She has been working hard, for days, without rest, without backup.

She is clutching the lifeless body of her brother. Delvin wears a tattered grey robe — cult robes — over the clothes he wore the day you all left the keep. His face is still. Not calm. Just finished. Whatever he saw at the end, he isn't seeing it anymore.

And from his open palm, loosening from fingers that have stopped gripping, with a dull, hollow thump against the cobblestones: a desiccated eyeball. It rolls to a stop against your boot. Even motionless, even disconnected from whatever powers it, it seems to be looking at something.
He went in. Three weeks ago. Said he'd found an entrance. Said he'd learned the phrase.
narrationBlocks.speaker: Kevori Fearnehart
narrationBlocks.emotion: Raw, looking up, eyes red, voice a blade

narrationBlocks.text: I searched for him every night. I found him here, twenty minutes ago. He was already cold.
narrationBlocks.speaker: Kevori Fearnehart
narrationBlocks.emotion: Grieving

narrationBlocks.text: No. But that doesn't matter right now. What matters is what they did to him. And what you're going to do about it.
narrationBlocks.speaker: Kevori Fearnehart
narrationBlocks.emotion: When asked if she is okay

narrationBlocks.text: Find the cult. Find what they did to him. And burn it to the ground.
narrationBlocks.speaker: Kevori Fearnehart
narrationBlocks.emotion: Exhausted, furious

narrationBlocks.text:
She looks at you. Exhausted. Grieving. Furious.

'Will you finish it?'

THIS IS THE OPENING OF 'NEST OF THE ELDRITCH EYE'.
From this point, run the adventure as written in the source material. Give this scene emotional weight — Kevori is the players' connection to what happened while they were gone. She is grief and rage in equal parts. She will not be left behind.

The desiccated eyeball is the adventure hook. It matches the description in the Nest sourcebook exactly.

choices.text: End Prologue (Begin Nest of the Eldritch Eye)
choices.consequence: The Death House prologue is complete.

Neverwinter.name: Neverwinter
Neverwinter.description: A large, cosmopolitan city on the Sword Coast of Faerûn (the Forgotten Realms), known as the 'Jewel of the North.' It is a major hub of civilization, commerce, and adventure. Many campaigns begin here or use it as a home base. Characters from various settings may have originated from Neverwinter before the Mists of Barovia snatched them away.
